item.title: DFS Project
item.description:
Organization: Atmospheric Sciences Research Center (ASRC), University at Albany
Period: 2025-Present
Funder: New York State Department of Financial Services (NYS DFS)

Contributing to Assessing Climate Exposure and Financial Impacts at the Census Tract Level in New York State, a collaboration between ASRC and the NYS Department of Financial Services. The project supports DFS in quantifying current and future climate-driven physical risks for regulated entities and vulnerable communities — including low-to-moderate income communities — across New York State.

item.title: WISER Project
item.description:
WISER (Center for Weather Innovation and Smart Energy and Resilience) is an NSF-funded Phase 1 Industry-University Cooperative Research Center (IUCRC) between the University at Albany and the University of Connecticut. The center bridges meteorological research and the energy industry to improve power grid efficiency, reliability, and resilience under changing climate conditions.

My work focuses on weather and forecasting model development, supporting research thrusts in outage and load resilience modeling and next-generation atmospheric forecasting for energy applications.

item.title: EU-SCORES (TU Delft)
item.description:
EU-SCORES (European Scalable Offshore Renewable Energy Sources) was a €45M Horizon 2020 initiative led by the Dutch Marine Energy Centre. The project demonstrated integrated offshore multi-source energy parks combining wind, wave, and solar technologies to improve grid stability and reduce the levelized cost of energy.

My role involved atmospheric and wind-resource modeling to support siting, performance estimation, and energy yield assessments for offshore co-located renewable systems across European coastal regions.
